newsitem.title: MEXICO: Texas-Mexico gasoline duct begins service.
newsitem.headline: Texas-Mexico gasoline duct begins service.

text.p: A 20-mile (33-km) gasoline duct linking a refinery in El Paso, Texas, to a distribution terminal in Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, began operations on Wednesday, the Mexican state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said.

The eight-inch duct, a joint project by Pemex and Chevron Corp, "will guarantee the delivery of petroleum products and tend to the growing demand in Ciudad Juarez toward the end of this decade," Pemex said in a statement.
The duct has the capacity to transport up to 25,000 barrels per day of gasoline and diesel, the statement said.
Pemex also boasted that the $13 million duct, built by Mexican construction firm Empresas ICA, will protect the environment and provide greater security.
During the past five years, gasoline transport across the border averaged 13,500 barrels a day, Pemex said.
